question: Do real opponents cause crop oversupply / market-price crashes distinct from the self_inflicted mechanism already diagnosed in Phase 3.4?
finding: MELON price crashes to $1-19 in BOTH wins (4/8) and losses (7/10) -- it is NOT a discriminating signal between winning and losing, because our OWN ~21-22 tile MELON-solo default is, by itself, almost always sufficient to crash MELON's price (T=300 depth) over a full 30-day season, REGARDLESS of what the opponent does. Real opponents were NEVER observed growing MELON at meaningful volume in any of the 18 episodes (all real opponents who grew crops chose WHEAT or STRAWBERRY) -- so the specific 'opponent floods MELON' mechanism Phase 3.3's ExpansionDetector targets (built from the SYNTHETIC expansion_oriented archetype) was NOT observed even once in this real sample. This does not mean it cannot happen against a real opponent, only that none of these 18 episodes exhibited it.
self_inflicted_crash_in_real_play: CONFIRMED to occur (in the sense that MELON price is low at game end in 11/18 real episodes), but re-characterized: it is a near-universal BACKGROUND CONDITION of playing MELON-solo for a full season, not a special adversarial event. It becomes DECISIVE only when the opponent happens to have chosen a crop whose price held up better (4 of the 10 losses, see failure_knowledge_base.json L004/L006/L007/L009) -- in the other 4 real wins and 7 real losses it does not appear to be the deciding factor at all (the scaling mechanism or opponent passivity dominates instead).
town_consumption_interactions: NOT separately analyzed this phase -- would require per-turn action-level reconstruction beyond the daily-checkpoint trajectories built here. Flagged as UNKNOWN, not assumed negligible.
confidence_label: SUPPORTED for the MELON-crash-is-universal finding (directly measured across all 18 episodes' final market prices); HYPOTHESIS for its role in the 4 'modest' losses.
